transcriber_notes: Low-resolution (1259x856) screenshot of a SnowPro-style Windows form; no app branding visible -> source_format 'other'. Printed date 08/12/2012 (D/M/Y as in other SnowPro screenshots) agrees with the file name. Height axis 2.7 px/cm with 10 cm gridlines, BUT the image is locally compressed between the 110 and 90 cm gridlines (46 px instead of 54; the 100 gridline is missing and the '100' label is cut) - heights above 110 read on the upper scale (150 at y300, surface line 141 at y324), below 90 on the lower scale (90 at y454, 0 at y697). No layer boundary falls in the compressed band. Boundaries 141/118/79/72/64/50/30/29/24/23/0 from bar edges and the H-column leader lines (+-0.5 cm). Table rows mapped to layers one-to-one through leader lines. Hardness axis non-linear (K, P, 1F, 4F, F at 216/108/54/27/~13 px from the bar origin; shear-stress axis 800/400/200 N/m2 below). Bars: F, 1F- (7 px past 1F), 1F, 1F+ (13 px past 1F), P, P, 1F, 1F+, P+ (thin line 40 px past P), P. The R-column icons (X = 1F, double slash = P, with +/- marks) agree with every bar reading. Second E column = size of the second (secondary) form. Temperatures: circle markers read on 13.5 px/deg C (0 C at the 4F/0 gridline, -20 at the leftmost gridline); the surface marker reads -13.3 while the printed Surface Temp is -13.0 (recorded as measured). The 100 cm point is a line kink inside the compressed band (height approximate); markers at 60-30 cm are inside the hatched bars (+-0.2 C). The dashed segment above the surface ends near the air temperature (-11.2) and is not a snow temperature.
